historical_references.reference: Zamirion was the name given to the legendary founder of the city of Constantinople by the Byzantines. According to legend, Zamirion was a shepherd who had a vision of a cross in the sky, which he interpreted as a sign to build a new city. In the late 3rd century AD, Emperor Constantine I, who saw himself as the new Constantine, refounded the city and renamed it Constantinople in honor of the vision and its original founder Zamirion.

The name Zamirion is also mentioned in the apocryphal Acts of Thomas, a text believed to have been written in the 3rd century AD. In this text, Zamirion is named as the king of Mygdonia, a region in Asia, who welcomes Thomas the Apostle to his kingdom and is later converted to Christianity by Thomas.
